gh-issue.description: GitHub issue: desc, comments, images, linked PRs. :full = no truncation, all comments. Targets another repo with a leading repo:OWNER/NAME op.

gh-issues.description: Issue triage board: list issues (no default author filter — the queue, not mine), ranked unrankable → external author → stale body → no linked PR → oldest. Per issue: linked-PR state from the timeline, external-filer marker from GitHub's authorAssociation, age, comment count, labels, stale-body flag (newest comment newer than lastEditedAt, or createdAt when the body was never edited). Enrichment is one GraphQL call per 20 issues; when it fails the derived fields render '?' and the footer names why — never 0, never 'internal', never 'no PR'. Filters (comma-sep): author/assignee/label/milestone/state. Flags: nopipe (skip enrichment), iids, external, stale.

gh-issue-create.description: Create a GitHub issue from a JSON/TOML payload file. Supports labels, assignees, and milestone (by title).

gh-pr.description: Review a pull request: branch, checks, reviews/approval, linked issue, diff stat, comments — the full dashboard. A truncated description says so twice — in the header and at the cut — with the exact char count withheld; :full uncaps it. :status = slim merge-state only (~250B, fits hook cache).

gh-prs.description: PR triage board: list PRs (default author=@me), sorted failing-first. Per PR: check rollup (failed→check name), approval (reviewDecision), age, diff size, watch-state, draft/conflict/threads flags + actionable footer. Filters (comma-sep): author/reviewer/assignee/label/state. Flags: nopipe (skip review-thread enrichment), iids, failed. The core board is one gh call; review threads enrich in parallel.

gh-run.description: What passed, what failed? Workflow run jobs with statuses and failed step names. Targets another repo with a leading repo:OWNER/NAME op.

gh-job.description: Why did this job fail? PR context + error pattern search + log tail. Takes EITHER id namespace: a check-run id (CodeQL, Dependabot, external CI) renders the check run — status, output, annotations — under '# Check run #N' with a 'Routed:' line naming the switch, so you never have to know which of GitHub's two lists a red leg landed in; the checks API is only consulted after the Actions endpoint 404s, so working calls cost nothing extra, and a checks call that does not answer declines rather than rendering an empty check. :fail (alias :errors) = matched failure blocks only, no tail — the tight triage view, per-job patterns; :raw dumps full trace; :raw:START[:END] slices lines (1-indexed, inclusive); :raw:-N is the last N lines; a START past the end returns the tail of the width requested and says so rather than declining; :grep:PATTERN ad-hoc regex over the log (literal fallback, context, tail on no-match; emission budgeted by GH_JOB_GREP_MAX_BYTES, default 65536 — a capped view says so in its header AND footer with an exact 'N of M matching lines shown' and names bytes, not a match limit, as what cut)

gh-check.description: What did this check run say? The *other* id namespace: CodeQL, Dependabot, code-scanning uploads and external CI report through the checks API, not through Actions, so gh-job 404s on their ids. gh-check:ID prints the check run's status, output title/summary and its annotations — path:line, title, message, which for a scanning check is the whole finding — capped at GH_CHECK_ANNOTATION_CAP (default 5) with a '+N more' disclosure in header AND footer. Zero annotations on a non-passing check is never rendered as an all-clear, and a failed annotations fetch is never rendered as zero. gh-check:pr:N lists the check runs on PR N's head commit with their ids, because gh-pr:N:status names a non-Actions leg without one. A 404 probes the Actions namespace and, when the id is a job, says so and names gh-job. Since #827 this is the explicit form rather than the only route — gh-job:ID answers for a check run too, and gh-pr names a non-Actions leg as 'CodeQL (check #ID)'. Does not read the code-scanning API.

gh-follow.description: Follow a GitHub user via the authenticated gh CLI session.

gh-following.description: List users you follow on GitHub.

gh-batch-follow.description: Follow each username from a file (one per line, '#' comments). Sleeps 1s between calls.

gh-star.description: Star a GitHub repository via gh CLI.

gh-batch-star.description: Star each OWNER/REPO from a file (one per line, '#' comments). Sleeps 1s between calls.

gh-find-followable.description: Discover candidate users to follow: pulls stargazers + contributors of a repo, dedupes, filters out orgs. Pipe to a file then review before gh-batch-follow.

gh-find-starable.description: Discover repos worth starring by topic. Pulls top N repos for the topic, sorted by stars. Pipe to a file then review before gh-batch-star.
